A second lesson

This lesson exists so that one check has a corpus to look at. The prompted-output rule asks what the rest of the content does with a token, so a single lesson cannot express it: the evidence that fetch is output rather than a command lives here, and the block that misuses it lives in the lesson before this one.

Update the package index. The tool prints a line for each repository it reaches.

$ example-tool packages update
fetch https://packages.example.com/aarch64/APKINDEX.tar.gz
fetch https://packages.example.com/x86_64/APKINDEX.tar.gz
OK: 12 packages available

Nothing else in this lesson is a finding. It is here to be read, not to be repaired, and the tests assert that it reports nothing of its own.
